label: prop1
title: Boolean functions of fixed mean with no almost-forcing sub-half-size coalition
difficulty_reason: The selected existence theorem requires constructing one Boolean function that simultaneously defeats every coalition of size at most (1/2−δ)n while keeping an arbitrary prescribed fixed mean. Section3 chooses a random CNF at the logarithmic clause-length scale and combines uniform coalition avoidance with a second-moment estimate for its density; the construction and simultaneous quantitative constraints are substantive obligations beyond ordinary qualification-exam concentration exercises.
review_note: The full mathematical article and original bibliography are retained, including the definitions of J_S^+, the random CNF construction, both supporting lemmas and the complete authored proof of Theorem1.1. Its source-local core lies in Section3; KKL and standard concentration facts remain accurately cited. Theorem1.2 has the separate exponential influence obstruction and ClaimsA–E, all retained as uncounted context in this prototype. Original source DOI metadata has a missing punctuation dot (toc2024 versus toc.2024); the current official landing page supplies DOI10.4086/toc.2024.v020a004, and publication/date/author/title/PDF identity match.
